verdicts.matching_evidence:
The central application to the Ijjas–Steinhardt (IS) cyclic model in Sec. 2 relies on an NEC-based argument that is not rigorously justified for the model in question. The proof assumes $dH/dt \leq 0$ throughout each cycle (except at idealized bounces) and extends bounds derived under this assumption across infinitely many cycles. However, the IS model crucially involves NEC violation for a non-singular bounce. The paper does not justify how the bounds hold globally despite NEC violation and discontinuities in $H(t)$.

Recommendation: Clarify explicitly in Sec. 2 which parts of each cycle satisfy the NEC and where it is violated in the IS model.

Sec. 2 models the bounce as a discontinuity in $H(t)$. The regularity of the spacetime and the extension of geodesics across such an idealized bounce is not discussed.
